context_requirements: Expression of TLR7 (or other TLRs) on the cell surface or in endosomes
For interferon and immunoproteasome genes, intact type I IFN signaling
For prostate lines, high TLR expression and PI3K-AKT/JAK-STAT coupling may enhance response
falsifiers: No induction of NFKBIA, NFKBIB, NFKBIE, RELB, NFKB2, or TICAM1 at 6 h in any line
No increase in interferon-stimulated genes (e.g., STAT1, PLSCR1, UBE2L6, HERC6) at 24 h
No change in antigen presentation genes (HLA-DRA, HLA-DMA, PSMB8, PSMB10, PSME1, PSME2) at 24 h
Strong and uniform up-regulation of proliferation genes at 24 h instead of the expected down-regulation
No difference in response between TLR7-high and TLR7-low lines

evidence.supports: TLR7 agonists induce a selected set of genes in human dendritic cells, often synergizing with other TLRs
TLR agonist combinations activate IL-12 and type I IFN pathways in T cells
TLR signaling in prostate cancer cells with high TLR expression flows through PI3K-AKT and JAK-STAT to OXPHOS and ROS

changes: Removed STAT1 from proximal_up because STAT1 is an interferon-signaling transcription factor induced downstream of type I IFN, not a direct TLR7/MyD88/TRIF proximal target; it remains in late_up.
Removed STAT1 from late_up duplicate placement is not needed; kept single late_up entry to avoid appearing in both proximal and late lists.
Kept NFKBIA/NFKBIB/NFKBIE/RELB/NFKB2/TICAM1 as proximal_up because TLR7-MyD88/TRIF-NF-kB signaling directly induces these negative feedback and NF-kB subunits.
Kept CXCL2/IL1B/CCL2/IER3/ZFP36/BIRC2/TNIP1/SQSTM1 as proximal_up because they are canonical NF-kB/AP-1 immediate early TLR targets.
Kept late_up interferon/antigen-presentation genes because type I IFN secondary response at 24 h is plausible for TLR7 in responsive lines.
Kept late_down proliferation genes because TLR-induced growth arrest at 24 h is plausible, though not universal across all lines.
Kept line_response weak for most lines and moderate for PC3/VCAP because retrieved evidence only supports high-TLR prostate cancer coupling, not broad responsiveness.
Kept kinetics slow and magnitude weak/moderate because TLR7 responses in non-immune adherent lines are typically delayed and modest.

Kept evidence PMID 15995707, 35340661, 39060412 because their abstracts support TLR7/TLR agonist gene induction, IFN/IL-12 pathway activation, and prostate cancer TLR-PI3K-AKT/JAK-STAT coupling respectively.
